newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farm machinery sales seen slowing in 1997.
newsitem.headline: French farm machinery sales seen slowing in 1997.

text.p: Demand for farm machinery in France may slow down in 1997 after rising for three consecutive years, manufacturers' union SYGMA predicted on Tuesday.
"We are hoping activity will remain sustained but with a trend towards a slowdown," SYGMA said in a statement.
French tractor registrations may drop to 33-34,000 units in 1997 from 37,571 in 1996, it predicted.

On the positive side SYGMA said EU farmers' income rose by almost five percent in 1996, reaching a 20-year high, while that of French farmers stabilised after rising sharply in the previous two years.

But uncertainties over the level of the new set-aside rate for the 1998 EU grain harvest and fears of possible changes to the EU Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) might hold up investment decisions, it said.
Sales of farm machinery on the French market rose by 14.5 percent to 23 billion francs in 1996 over 1995. This included six billion francs of imports.
Sales of French farm machinery at home and abroad rose nine percent to 16.5 billion francs.
SYGMA linked the performance mostly to a rise of 10 percent in French farmers' income in 1994 and of 11.5 percent in 1995.
